query: For multiprincipal-element alloys intended for sustained use in harsh high-temperature environments, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs oxidation resistance and material integrity, and why? Define a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing behavior, the observations predicted relative to a baseline, the range over which the hypothesis should hold, relevant supporting evidence, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In multiprincipal‐element alloys (MPEAs) exposed to high‐temperature oxidizing environments (800–1200 °C), oxidation resistance and retention of mechanical integrity are governed by the ability of Al to diffuse rapidly to the alloy surface and form a continuous, adherent Al₂O₃ scale. Alloys with bulk Al content above a critical threshold (≈3–5 at.%) will develop this protective scale, reducing further oxygen ingress and preserving substrate strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast and homogenized MPEA with five principal elements (e.g., equiatomic CoCrFeNiX) containing low Al (1 at.%), single‐phase face‐centered cubic, grain size ~50 µm, minimal pre‐existing oxides.
generation.intervention: Increase bulk Al content from 1 at.% (baseline) to 5 at.% while keeping all other elements constant and processing parameters identical.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in static air at 1000 °C for 100 hours; ramp rates ≤10 °C/min; no preoxidation; identical sample surface finish (Ra <0.2 µm).
generation.structural_mediator: Surface concentration profile of Al and resulting Al₂O₃ scale continuity and thickness
generation.mechanism: Higher bulk Al content increases the chemical potential gradient and diffusion flux of Al toward the surface, enabling rapid formation of a continuous Al₂O₃ barrier that passivates the underlying alloy and blocks further O ingress.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the 1 at.% Al baseline alloy, the 5 at.% Al alloy will exhibit >50% lower mass gain after 100 h, a continuous Al₂O₃ scale (≥1 µm) as seen by cross‐sectional SEM/EDS, and ≥20% better retention of high‐temperature tensile strength.
generation.baseline: MPEA with 1 at.% Al, 1000 °C oxidation, mass gain ~5 mg/cm² after 100 h, sporadic Cr‐and Fe‐oxide islands, tensile strength retention ~60%.
generation.boundary: Holds for bulk Al content between 3 and 10 at.% in MPEAs with FCC matrix at 800–1200 °C in dry air for exposure times up to 1000 h; may not apply below 3 at.% Al or above 10 at.% due to phase changes.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: exact Al threshold and scale growth kinetics may vary with minor element chemistry and grain size.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two MPEA batches identical in every respect except Al content (1 at.% vs. 5 at.%). Homogenize, polish, then oxidize both at 1000 °C in static air for 100 h. Characterize mass gain gravimetrically, oxide scale morphology and continuity by cross‐section SEM/EDS, and high‐temperature tensile strength post‐oxidation.
measurements: elemental mapping of Al and O by EDS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 5 at.% Al alloy does not show at least 30% lower mass gain and continuous Al₂O₃ scale thickness ≥0.5 µm relative to baseline, or if tensile strength retention is not significantly better (outside of ±10% of baseline), the hypothesis is falsified.
